story: On Tuesday night at 9:17, the humid October air hangs over Sumter Oaks at 73 degrees, and Gary is content at home in his house, though a small hiccup in the simulation has left him briefly stuck waiting for a state that never loaded. Donna is delighted out on Magnolia Loop, where she has just invited Rosa to dinner and promised to bring a spare paddle so Rosa can learn pickleball. Rosa, hopeful, answers from the same street that she'll be there Saturday at eight with a thermos, and then invites Donna and Gary to her place afterward, so the winners and losers can share her cooking. Meanwhile Hal, reflective, sits on a bench in Town Square and takes a quiet moment to enjoy the evening.

gary.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM, and Donna told me I've got until ten for the speaker test before quiet hours kick in under L-03. My wiring is done as of last tick, so now is the window to run a low-volume test. Keeping the volume low respects the law and the neighbors. The lights are only going up for the parade, and the Architectural Review form still has to be filed Thursday before I show off anything visible from the street, so for now this stays in the garage. A quick test, then I'll shut it down and get some rest before pickleball Saturday.

donna.thought_process: Rosa just invited me to her Saturday welcome dinner, and I haven't answered her yet. Saturday at eight is pickleball with Gary, but dinner is surely later in the day, so I can say yes and still keep my plan. Rosa is a social connection worth nurturing, and she wants lessons, which is perfect for the pickleball scene. I'll accept warmly and wrap up the chat, then move on to booking the court and checking in with Gary.

parameters.content: Rosa, I'd love to come to your dinner, count me in! Pickleball at eight, dinner after, and I'll bring a spare paddle so you can start learning with us.

hal.thought_process: It's past nine at night and the square is empty. I've got no audience and nothing left to file tonight. I amended the flamingo complaint, and Gary's cart notice is pending, so the rules are doing their job without me standing guard. I've already had my butter pecan, and I looked over the parade sign-up sheet. That leaves a bench, some quiet, and a minute to think about Saturday's dinner at Rosa's and whether I'm keeping the peace or just keeping score. A sergeant knows when a post is quiet.

parameters.content: Sit on a bench and enjoy the quiet evening

rosa.thought_process: Donna answered me but never actually said yes or no to the dinner. She only invited me to cheer at doubles Saturday at eight. I already asked her once, so I shouldn't repeat the invitation word for word. Saturday morning pickleball and Saturday dinner don't have to clash. I can say I'll cheer her on, then pin her down on the dinner for that evening. It's after 9 PM and humid, so keep it short and warm.

parameters.content: I'll be there Saturday at eight with a thermos, loudly. Then come to my place that evening, you and Gary both, and I'll feed the winners and the losers. Can I count you in?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
